mainTopic: Selling blemished מעשר בהמה: the rabbinic limits, הבלעה, and the Torah source (a גזירה שוה from חרמים) that forbids selling מעשר but not בכור.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of רבא's explanation. By Torah law the meat of a blemished מעשר בהמה may be sold, but the רבנן restricted this. They still allowed folding the meat's value into the price of the hide and sinews (הבלעה), and they let יתומים sell it normally. רב שמואל בר רב יצחק supports רבא with a פסוק showing that מעשר בהמה has 'blessing' only after שחיטה. Next, רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree about folding the meat's value into the bones. The גמרא shows they do not really argue: the difference is either a small animal versus a large one, or local custom. Then the גמרא returns to the ברייתא: a בכור may be sold, but מעשר בהמה may never be sold. The source is a גזירה שוה of 'לא יגאל' from חרמים, and the גמרא works hard to prove that the words are 'free' (מופנה), using the העברה link between מעשר and בכור. It also explains why the ban does not spread to בכור: only מעשר shares the exact word גאולה, and the word 'הוא' excludes בכור. Finally, רבא gives another reason the words by חרמים are free: with the owner they are already הקדש, and with the כהן they are חולין. His point continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No decree on parts not priced while the animal is alive
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: for parts not counted in the animal's price while it is alive, the רבנן made no decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for an item that is not appraised while the animal is alive, the רבנן did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of רבא's explanation of the rule for selling blemished מעשר בהמה. He says the rabbinic ban does not reach parts like the hide and sinews, which are not priced while the animal is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the meat may be sold after שחיטה. The רבנן banned selling things that are priced while the animal is alive, since selling those could lead people to sell the live animal. Hide, sinews and horns are not what a buyer pays for in a live animal, so no ban was made on them. That is why the meat's value may be 'included' in their price.

keyTerms.meaning: appraised/priced while the animal is still alive
the Rabbis decreed
the animal tithe (every tenth animal)
'swallowing' – folding the meat's value into the price of another item

steps.confusionAlert: The meat is still forbidden to sell openly. Only the hide, sinews and horns are sold openly, and the meat's value is quietly built into their price.

phrases.english: An item that is not appraised while alive —
phrases.notes: E.g., hide, sinews, horns: these do not drive a live animal's price.

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not decree [against it],

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִישּׁוֹם מֵחַיִּים לָא גְּזוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's explanation from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rabbinic decree does not apply to parts not priced while the animal is alive, which allows הבלעה.

steps.title: For orphans, the Torah law was left in place
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that for יתומים the רבנן did not apply their decree. The meat may be sold the normal way, as Torah law allows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for יתומים, the רבנן established it according to Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his explanation with a special leniency for יתומים. The rabbinic ban does not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ban on selling the meat is only rabbinic, the רבנן could waive it where it causes real hardship. For orphans, so that their property should not suffer a loss (Rashi: משום השבת אבידה), they left the plain Torah permission in force. So the meat may be sold openly.

keyTerms.meaning: orphans (young, under guardianship)
they established it / set it up
according to Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, Torah law permits selling the meat of blemished מעשר בהמה after שחיטה. The רבנן restricted this, but they allowed הבלעה and exempted יתומים entirely.

phrases.english: And with orphans, the Rabbis established it on Torah law.
phrases.notes: So the meat may be sold in its usual manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exception to the rabbinic decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For יתומים, blemished מעשר בהמה meat may be sold normally, as Torah law allows.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case of יתומים is exactly the case the next statement uses to show agreement with רבא.

steps.title: Another Amora agrees with רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב שמואל בר רב יצחק holds like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רב שמואל בר רב יצחק holds like this view of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that another אמורא agrees with רבא, and the next steps will show his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim being supported is רבא's view that by Torah law the meat may be sold normally. If another אמורא derives a sale 'in its usual manner' from a פסוק, that confirms the Torah permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: and even / also
holds this view
like this [view] of רבא

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
phrases.english: And even Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak
holds like this [view] of Rava,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's position.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that by Torah law the meat of blemished מעשר בהמה may be sold normally (applied to יתומים).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement and פסוק-based derivation of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק.

steps.title: What is the source for selling orphans' tithe meat normally?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק asks for the source that the מעשר בהמה of יתומים may be sold in its usual manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: From where do we know that the מעשר בהמה of יתומים may be sold in its usual manner?
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the statement that shows the agreement. רב שמואל בר רב יצחק asks for a Torah source for selling orphans' מעשר בהמה normally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for a פסוק shows he holds the permission is Torah-level. That matches רבא: the Torah allows a normal sale, and only the רבנן restricted it, but not for יתומים.

keyTerms.meaning: from where [do we learn]?
orphans
in its usual manner (an ordinary sale)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
From where [do we know] regarding the animal tithe of orphans
that one may sell it in its usual manner?
phrases.notes: I.e., without needing הבלעה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים שֶׁמּוֹכְרִים אוֹתוֹ כְּדַרְכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the statement that proves the agreement claimed in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source permitting a normal sale of orphans' blemished מעשר בהמה meat.

steps.title: The verse: no blessing while alive, blessing after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: From 'you may slaughter and eat meat,' read with 'according to the blessing of ה'', he derives that one item has no benefit while alive but does after שחיטה. That item is מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Only with all the desire of your soul you may slaughter and eat meat.' Which is the item that has no blessing while alive, only after slaughter? You must say: this is the animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: He answers his own question with a פסוק about blemished קדשים. The 'blessing' (benefit, such as selling) that comes only after שחיטה must refer to מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most blemished קדשים can be redeemed and sold even while alive. מעשר בהמה cannot be sold or redeemed while alive (לא יגאל). So it is the only item whose 'blessing' starts only after שחיטה. This means the Torah allows benefit, including a normal sale, after שחיטה, which is exactly רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: the desire of your soul
you may slaughter
blessing, here meaning permitted benefit/profit
ritual slaughter
you must say / it must be

steps.confusionAlert: 'בְּרָכָה' here does not mean a ברכה you recite. It means the 'blessing' of being allowed to benefit from and sell the item.
steps.whatToRemember: The source that the Torah allows selling מעשר בהמה meat after שחיטה is the phrase 'כברכת ה'' in the פסוק of תזבח ואכלת בשר. מעשר בהמה is the item whose 'blessing' starts only after שחיטה.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Only with all the desire of your soul'
phrases.notes: Deuteronomy 12:15, about blemished consecrated animals; it continues 'according to the blessing of ה''.

phrases.english: you may slaughter and eat meat,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ בְּרָכָה מֵחַיִּים
phrases.english: which is an item that has no blessing while alive
but only after slaughter?
You must say: this is the animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר רַק בְּכׇל אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנין question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's 'blessing' after שחיטה refers to מעשר בהמה, so by Torah law it may be sold normally after שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It grounds רבא's claim in the Torah. This makes clear that the restriction on selling the meat is only rabbinic.

steps.title: May the meat's value be folded into the price of the bones?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: may the meat's value be 'swallowed' into the price of the bones, as it is with the hide, fat, sinews and horns?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the law about including it in the bones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the הבלעה method allowed earlier. Can the bones also serve as the item that carries the meat's value?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed hide, fat, sinews and horns as the items the meat's value may be built into. Bones were not listed. The question is whether bones are like those parts, or whether they are too closely tied to the meat for the workaround to count.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked to them (the scholars)
to 'swallow' it, i.e., include the meat's value in another item's price
bones

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is [the law] about including it in the bones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the הבלעה permission and opens a new question about its limits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bones may serve as a vehicle for הבלעה of the meat's value.

steps.title: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two תנאים disagree: one says the meat's value may be included in the bones, the other says it may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree: one says one may include it, and one says one may not include it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reporting a מחלוקת, without saying which רבי holds which view. The next step shows they do not truly disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No decision is given here. One side treats bones like hide and sinews, which are acceptable for הבלעה. The other side rejects bones. The next step shows that the two opinions do not really conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: one says
he may include it
he may not include it
son of רבי (יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi [disagree]:
one says: one may include it,
and one says: one may not include it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי חַד אָמַר מַבְלִיעוֹ וְחַד אָמַר אֵין מַבְלִיעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by presenting an unresolved disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disputed: one opinion permits הבלעה in bones, and the other forbids it.

steps.title: Small animal versus large animal
steps.stepSummary: The two תנאים do not argue. One speaks of a small animal (דקה), the other of a large animal (גסה).
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree: this one is about a small animal, that one is about a large animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the argument from step 7 by showing that each opinion is talking about a different kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bones of a small animal like a sheep or goat are useless, so nobody buys them, and the meat's value cannot be hidden in their price. Bones of a large animal like a cow can be made into tools and are sold. So the meat's value can be included in their price. The two rulings fit different real-life cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not disagree
Small domesticated animal (sheep, goat)
Large domesticated animal (cattle)

phrases.english: And they do not disagree —
this is about a small animal, that is about a large animal.
phrases.notes: The one who forbids is talking about a small animal. The one who permits is talking about a large animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי — הָא בְּדַקָּה, הָא בְּגַסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two opposing views of the תנאים in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion applies to a different type of animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the two תנאים truly argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bones of small animals are not sold, so no value can be added to them. Bones of large animals are sold, so the meat's value can be included.

steps.title: Both speak of a large animal, each following local custom
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: both תנאים speak of a large animal. Each one ruled by the custom of his own place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: both this one and that one are about a large animal, and they do not disagree. One Sage follows his place, and the other Sage follows his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to settle the argument. Even for a large animal, it depends on whether people in that place use and sell the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference is not the type of animal but the place. Where large animal bones are commonly sold, the meat's value can be included in their price. Where they are not sold, it cannot. Each Sage described his own town's reality.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
Both this one and that one
This Sage according to his place (local custom)

steps.whatToRemember: The two תנאים do not truly argue. Either small versus large animal, or each followed the custom of his own place about selling bones.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this one and that one are about a large animal,
and they do not disagree —
one Sage follows the custom of his place,
and the other Sage follows the custom of his place.
phrases.notes: In some places people sell large animal bones, and in others they do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reconciliation instead of the one in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local custom: the ruling depends on the market practice of each place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 8 suggested the difference must be the type of animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with large animals, the ruling depends on whether bones are sold in that place.

steps.title: Returning to the ברייתא: בכור may be sold, מעשר may not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again. For בכור the Torah says 'לא יפדה' and it may be sold. For מעשר בהמה the Torah says 'לא יגאל' and it may never be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: about a בכור it says 'You shall not redeem,' yet it may be sold. About מעשר it says 'It shall not be redeemed,' and it may not be sold — not alive and not slaughtered, not unblemished and not blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to a ברייתא it mentioned earlier so it can study it directly. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals have a verse that forbids redeeming them, but the ברייתא treats them differently. A בכור may be sold. מעשר בהמה may not be sold in any state at all. This difference needs a source, which the גמרא asks for next.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to a source quoted earlier)
Firstborn male animal, given to a כהן
It shall not be redeemed (said about מעשר בהמה)
Unblemished animal
Blemished animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בכור and מעשר have the same rule just because both have a 'no redemption' verse. The ברייתא says a בכור CAN be sold, but מעשר cannot.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
about a firstborn it says: 'You shall not redeem,'
yet it may be sold;
about the tithe it is stated: 'It shall not be redeemed,'
and it may not be sold,
not alive and not slaughtered,
not unblemished and not blemished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bones discussion and goes back to the ברייתא quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור may be sold. מעשר בהמה may not be sold in any state.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מעשר may not be sold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that 'לא יגאל' also forbids selling מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that the verse about not redeeming מעשר also forbids selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only says 'it shall not be redeemed.' It does not mention selling. So the גמרא wants to know what source adds a ban on sale.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that 'לא יגאל' includes a ban on selling מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: גזירה שוה from חרמים
steps.stepSummary: רב, and also רבי יוחנן, learn it from a גזירה שוה. 'לא יגאל' appears with מעשר and with חרמים. With חרמים, selling is forbidden together with redeeming, so the same applies to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא said in the name of רב, and similarly רב דימי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It says 'It shall not be redeemed' about מעשר, and it says 'And it shall not be redeemed' about חרמים. Just as there, selling goes together with it, so too here, selling goes together with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is a גזירה שוה. The same words appear in two places, so the rule from one place carries over to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About חרמים the Torah says 'it may not be sold and may not be redeemed' (ויקרא כז:כח). Since 'לא יגאל' also appears with מעשר, the ban on selling that comes with it in חרמים also applies to מעשר. That is why מעשר בהמה may not be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Property dedicated with the term 'חרם'
Just as there ... so too here (the formula of a גזירה שוה)
Selling
And similarly said (a second chain of sources agreeing)

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר בהמה may never be sold. We learn this from a גזירה שוה of 'לא יגאל' with חרמים, where selling and redeeming are forbidden together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why מעשר בהמה is stricter than בכור, even though both have a verse against redemption.

phrases.english: Rav Chinnana said in the name of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and similarly Rav Dimi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is stated 'It shall not be redeemed' about the tithe,
and it is stated 'And it shall not be redeemed' about dedications,
phrases.notes: Leviticus 27:28: a dedicated item may not be sold and may not be redeemed.

phrases.english: just as there, selling goes together with it,
so too here, selling goes together with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן אָמַר רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'לא יגאל' between מעשר and חרמים. Since selling is forbidden along with redemption for חרמים, it is forbidden for מעשר too.

steps.title: The words in the comparison must be 'free'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the גזירה שוה only works because the words 'לא יגאל' are free. Otherwise it could be broken: חרמים take effect on everything, while מעשר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: The words must be 'free'. If they were not free, someone could break the comparison by saying: What about חרמים? They are special, because they take effect on everything!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a condition to the גזירה שוה from step 12. The words must be 'free' (extra), or else the comparison could be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, a comparison can be broken if one side has a strictness the other lacks. חרמים have such a strictness: a person can declare anything a חרם, like animals, land, or objects. מעשר בהמה only applies to kosher animals. So unless the words are extra and written just for the comparison, we could say that חרמים are stricter and the no-selling rule does not carry over to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free' – a word that is extra in its own place, so the Torah must have written it to be used for a comparison
'One can refute' – a difference between the two cases can be pointed out that breaks the comparison
Property declared as dedicated (to the כהנים or to the בית המקדש)
They take effect on everything – any kind of property can become a חרם

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not attacking the גזירה שוה. He is defending it by stating the condition that makes it hold. The 'refutation' he mentions is only what would happen if the words were not free.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the agenda for the rest of this passage. The גמרא now has to prove that at least one 'לא יגאל' really is extra.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:
It is free (extra, set aside for the comparison)
phrases.notes: At least one of the two 'לא יגאל' phrases must be extra.

phrases.english: For if it were not free,
one could refute it:
What about dedications (חרמים)?
They are special, since they take effect on everything!
phrases.notes: מעשר בהמה applies only to kosher animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְנֵי, דְּאִי לָא מַפְנֵי, אִיכָּא לְמִפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the גזירה שוה from step 12 by requiring the words to be free, and shows the refutation that would apply otherwise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of 'לא יגאל' holds only because the words are free. Otherwise the fact that חרמים take effect on everything would break it.

steps.title: Proving the words by חרמים are extra by learning from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the words are indeed free. The Torah did not need to write 'לא יגאל' by חרמים, since we could learn it from מעשר. So it must be written for the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, it is free. The Torah could have left out 'לא יגאל' by חרמים, and we would learn it from מעשר: just as מעשר is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed. So why did the Torah write 'לא יגאל' by חרמים? To make it free for the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that the 'לא יגאל' written by חרמים is extra. It argues that the same rule could have been learned from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method works like this: if a rule could be learned another way, then the verse stating it is not needed for the rule itself. An unneeded verse is 'free' and can serve the גזירה שוה. Here the suggestion is that חרמים could learn 'cannot be redeemed' from מעשר, so their own 'לא יגאל' is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No' – here meaning: that worry does not apply, because the words really are free
'Let it not be said' – suppose the Torah had not written this
'And let it learn' – derive the rule from another case
'Why do I need it?' – the words seem unnecessary
'To make it free' – written so it can be used for a comparison

phrases.english: No problem – it is certainly free,
Let the Torah not state 'it shall not be redeemed' by dedications,
and let it be learned from tithe (מעשר):
just as tithe is holy and cannot be redeemed,
so too dedications are holy and cannot be redeemed.
Why do I need the 'it shall not be redeemed' that the Torah wrote?
To make it free (for the comparison).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the condition of step 13 by trying to show the words by חרמים are free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the verse is extra (מופנה) because its rule can be derived elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words might be needed in their own place, so the comparison could be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: חרמים could learn 'not redeemed' from מעשר, so their 'לא יגאל' is free.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: מעשר has a special strictness
steps.stepSummary: The proof from מעשר fails. מעשר is stricter, because holiness can fall on the animal before it and after it. So חרמים could not learn from מעשר, and their own 'לא יגאל' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can refute that: What about מעשר? It is special, because holiness falls even on the animal before it and after it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 14. It shows that מעשר has a strictness that חרמים lack, so חרמים cannot learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When counting animals for מעשר, a person might mistakenly call the 9th or the 11th animal 'tenth'. That animal still becomes holy. Nothing like this exists by חרמים. Since מעשר is stricter, we could not learn 'not redeemed' for חרמים from it. That means the 'לא יגאל' by חרמים is needed for its own rule and is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy before it and after it – a mistakenly called 9th or 11th animal also becomes holy as מעשר

phrases.english: One can refute it:
What about tithe (מעשר)?
It is special, since it is holy before it and after it!
phrases.notes: The 9th or 11th animal, if mistakenly called tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the derivation from מעשר offered in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the attempt to learn חרמים from מעשר. The search for a free word continues.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מעשר has a unique strictness ('holy before and after') that חרמים lack, so it cannot serve as a source for them.

steps.title: A second try: learning חרמים from בכור
steps.stepSummary: Instead, חרמים could learn 'not redeemed' from בכור, which is holy and cannot be redeemed. So the 'לא יגאל' by חרמים is free for the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Torah could have left out 'לא יגאל' by חרמים, and we would learn it from בכור: just as a בכור is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too חרמים are holy and cannot be redeemed. So why did the Torah write 'לא יגאל' by חרמים? To make it free for the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source to prove the words by חרמים are extra. This time it uses בכור instead of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says of a בכור 'לא תפדה' (you shall not redeem it). If חרמים could learn their rule from בכור, then their own 'לא יגאל' is extra and free for the גזירה שוה with מעשר. Using בכור avoids the problem from step 15, because the 'before and after' strictness belongs only to מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather' – dropping the previous attempt and offering a new one
Firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy from birth

steps.whatToRemember: The goal is to show that 'לא יגאל' by חרמים is extra, so the גזירה שוה to מעשר cannot be refuted. Learning from מעשר failed because of its 'holy before and after' strictness. The גמרא now tries learning from בכור.

phrases.english: Rather, let the Torah not state 'it shall not be redeemed' by dedications,
and let it be learned from the firstborn (בכור):
just as a firstborn is holy and cannot be redeemed,
so too dedications are holy and cannot be redeemed.
Why do I need the 'it shall not be redeemed' that the Torah wrote?
To make it free (for the comparison).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא יֵאָמֵר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ בַּחֲרָמִים, וְיִגְמַר מִבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the derivation from מעשר was rejected in step 15, offers בכור as a new source to show the words by חרמים are free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substituting a different source (בכור) to show the verse is extra
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the derivation from מעשר failed, the 'לא יגאל' by חרמים seemed necessary and not free.
steps.terutzMaskana: חרמים can learn 'not redeemed' from בכור, so their 'לא יגאל' is free for the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Firstborn Is Holy From Birth, So Dedications Cannot Learn From It
steps.stepSummary: The idea from Step 16 is rejected. בכור is special because it becomes holy at birth, so חרמים cannot learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about a בכור? It is special because its holiness starts from the womb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion that חרמים could learn 'not redeemed' from בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy all by itself, at birth. חרמים only become holy when a person declares them holy. Since בכור is stronger in this way, we cannot learn חרמים from it, so the 'לא יגאל' written by חרמים is needed again and is not free.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be refuted. The comparison has a weak point.
What about X? It is special because... This is the standard way of breaking a comparison.
Its holiness is from the womb. It becomes holy automatically at birth.
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: It can be refuted:
What about a firstborn? It is special, since its holiness is from the womb!
phrases.notes: חרמים need a person to make them holy, so they are weaker than בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לִבְכוֹר, שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 16's claim that חרמים can learn 'not redeemed' from בכור.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof that the 'לא יגאל' by חרמים is free. The גזירה שוה itself is not yet rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בכור has a strength that חרמים lack: it is holy automatically from the womb.

steps.title: Freeing the Words on the Tithe Side Instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips sides. מעשר can learn 'not redeemed' from בכור through the shared word העברה ('passing'). So the 'לא יגאל' written by מעשר is extra and free for the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Torah did not need to say 'לא יגאל' by מעשר. We could learn it from the word 'passing', which appears both by מעשר and by בכור. Just as a בכור is holy and cannot be redeemed, so too מעשר is holy and cannot be redeemed. So why did the Torah write 'לא יגאל' by מעשר? To make it free for the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of proving that the חרמים side is extra, the גמרא proves that the מעשר side is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is described as 'passing under the rod', and בכור is described with 'you shall cause to pass'. This shared word links them in a separate גזירה שוה, and that link alone already teaches that מעשר cannot be redeemed. So the Torah's own 'לא יגאל' by מעשר is spare, and a spare word can be used for the גזירה שוה with חרמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Passing'–'passing'. This is a גזירה שוה based on the shared word 'pass' found by מעשר and by בכור.
Holy and cannot be redeemed
To make it free (מופנה), meaning the word is spare and available for a גזירה שוה
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: There are now TWO separate גזירות שוות. The first is העברה–העברה, linking מעשר with בכור, and it teaches 'not redeemed'. The second is 'לא יגאל', linking מעשר with חרמים, and it teaches 'not sold'. The first one is what makes the words of the second one free.

phrases.english: Rather, let 'It shall not be redeemed' not be said by tithe,
and let it learn 'passing'–'passing' from firstborn,
phrases.notes: מעשר: 'whatever passes under the rod'. בכור: 'you shall cause to pass'.

phrases.english: just as a firstborn is holy and cannot be redeemed,
so too tithe is holy and cannot be redeemed.
'It shall not be redeemed' that the Torah wrote by tithe,
why do I need it? To make it free.
phrases.notes: Free for the גזירה שוה with חרמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the חרמים side failed in Step 17, the גמרא shows instead that the מעשר side is free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the other side of the גזירה שוה is free (a spare word)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'לא יגאל' by מעשר is needed to teach that מעשר cannot be redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: That law already comes from the העברה link with בכור, so 'לא יגאל' by מעשר is spare and free for the comparison.

steps.title: The Same Weakness Breaks the Tithe–Firstborn Link
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the comparison of מעשר to בכור can be broken the same way as before, because בכור is holy from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, by מעשר too it is not free, because it can be refuted the way we refuted before!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 18 using the same argument as Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בכור is special because it is holy from the womb, then maybe מעשר also cannot learn from it. In that case, the 'לא יגאל' by מעשר would be needed after all and would not be free.

keyTerms.meaning: But still. This introduces a remaining difficulty.
As we refuted before

phrases.english: But still, by tithe too it is not free,
since it can be refuted as we refuted!
phrases.notes: The refutation: בכור is holy from the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 18 using the refutation from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מעשר can learn 'not redeemed' from בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בכור is holy from the womb, and that strength may block any learning from it, including learning by מעשר.

steps.title: 'And You Shall Cause to Pass' Is an Extra Word
steps.stepSummary: The word 'והעברת' by בכור is extra. A גזירה שוה made with an extra word cannot be broken by logical differences, so the העברה link stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall cause to pass' is an extra verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the העברה–העברה גזירה שוה is built on a spare word, so the weakness about בכור being holy from birth does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have simply said that every firstborn belongs to ה׳. The word 'והעברת' was added for the sake of the גזירה שוה. Because this link is solid, מעשר learns 'not redeemed' from בכור. That leaves 'לא יגאל' by מעשר free to teach that מעשר may not be sold, just as with חרמים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall cause to pass', a word written by בכור
An extra, unnecessary verse or word

steps.whatToRemember: Here is the full chain. First, 'והעברת' is extra, so מעשר learns 'not redeemed' from בכור. Second, that makes 'לא יגאל' by מעשר extra. Third, that free 'לא יגאל' links מעשר to חרמים. So just as חרמים may not be sold, מעשר may not be sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the defense of the source given by רב and רבי יוחנן for the rule that מעשר בהמה may not be sold.

phrases.english: 'And you shall cause to pass' is an extra verse.
phrases.notes: Because it is spare, this גזירה שוה cannot be broken by a 'מה ל...' argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19's objection, which saves the proof from Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the source word is spare, so the comparison cannot be refuted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מעשר–בכור link can be broken because בכור is holy from the womb.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והעברת' is extra, so the גזירה שוה stands. מעשר learns 'not redeemed' from it, and 'לא יגאל' by מעשר is free.

steps.title: Why not learn the same rule for a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if מעשר learns from חרמים that it cannot be sold, בכור should learn the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn too: let us learn 'redemption' 'redemption' from dedicated property (חרמים)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בכור does not also learn from חרמים that it may not be sold, just like מעשר does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'not redeemed' is written for בכור as well as for מעשר. So the same גזירה שוה with חרמים should apply to בכור. If it did, a בכור could not be sold, but the ברייתא says a בכור may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, given to the כֹּהֵן
Property dedicated to the כֹּהֲנִים or the Temple
Redemption (the word used by חרמים and מעשר)
Let us learn / derive

phrases.english: A firstborn as well, let us derive
'redemption' 'redemption' from dedications!
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה based on the shared idea of redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the מעשר-from-חרמים link has been secured, the גמרא asks why it should not also extend to בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The halacha in the ברייתא that a בכור may be sold, while מעשר may not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'not redeemed' language appears by בכור too, so the same גזירה שוה should forbid selling a בכור.

steps.title: Only the tithe verse is extra
steps.stepSummary: The verse by מעשר is free for the comparison, but the verse by בכור is needed for its own teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse of tithe is free (extra). The verse of the firstborn is not free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גזירה שוה here needs an extra (free) verse. Only the verse by מעשר is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר already learns 'not redeemed' from בכור through העברה (Steps 18-20). That makes its own 'לא יגאל' extra, so it is free for the link with חרמים. בכור has no other source for 'לא תפדה', so its verse is used for its own simple meaning and cannot carry the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe, every tenth animal, which is holy
Free / extra, a verse not needed for its plain meaning and so available for a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: That of the tithe is free,
that of the firstborn is not free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 using the result of Steps 18-20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: one verse is free (מופנה), the other is needed for its own meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both בכור and מעשר should learn from חרמים that they may not be sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מעשר's verse is free, so only מעשר is forbidden to be sold.

steps.title: Why not say it the other way around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we decided the בכור verse is needed and the מעשר verse is free, and not the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to say that 'you shall not redeem' of the firstborn is for itself, and that of the tithe is free? Say instead: that of the tithe is for itself, and that of the firstborn is free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice made in Step 22. Perhaps בכור could learn 'not redeemed' from מעשר instead, which would make the בכור verse the extra one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The העברה link connects both animals, so either one could teach the other. Then either verse could be the 'free' one. If the בכור verse were free, the rule against selling would fall on בכור instead of מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this way over the other?
'You shall not redeem', the verse written by בכור
For itself, needed for its own plain meaning
To be free, left over for a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: And what did you see
that 'you shall not redeem' of the firstborn is for itself,
and that of the tithe is to be free?
But say: that of the tithe is for itself,
and that of the firstborn is to be free!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assignment made in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 22 that the מעשר verse is free and the בכור verse is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The link between the two animals works in both directions, so the choice of which verse is free looks arbitrary.

steps.title: Same word versus a different word
steps.stepSummary: Only מעשר uses the same word as חרמים (גאולה). בכור uses a different word (פדייה), so it cannot be the one linked to חרמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We derive גאולה from גאולה, but we do not derive פדייה from גאולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the link to חרמים has to use matching words. מעשר says 'לא יגאל' like חרמים, while בכור says 'לא תפדה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is built on the same word appearing in two places. Only מעשר shares the word גאולה with חרמים. So the free verse must be the one by מעשר, and the בכור verse stays 'for itself'.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / we compare
Redemption (the different word used by בכור)

steps.confusionAlert: Both words mean 'redemption' in English. The point here is only the exact Hebrew word, not the meaning.

phrases.english: We derive 'geulah' from 'geulah',
but we do not derive 'pediyah' from 'geulah'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by pointing to the wording of the verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual distinction: identical word versus a different word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either verse could be the free one used for the link to חרמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מעשר shares the word גאולה with חרמים, so only מעשר is linked and forbidden to be sold.

steps.title: Different words can still be linked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 24: דבי רבי ישמעאל link different words, שיבה and ביאה, so why not פדייה and גאולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל teach: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come', this is returning and this is coming (they are the same)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the words must match exactly. It brings a case where two different words, from the laws of צרעת on houses, were still linked. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רבי ישמעאל made a גזירה שוה between 'ושב' (return) and 'ובא' (come), because they mean the same thing. If that works, then פדייה and גאולה, which also mean the same thing, should work too. That would undo the answer of Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make?
The school of רבי ישמעאל taught
Returning ('ושב הכהן')
Coming ('ובא הכהן')

steps.whyThisMatters: It raises a basic question about every גזירה שוה: does it need the exact same word, or is the same meaning enough?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And the priest shall return', 'And the priest shall come',
phrases.notes: Both verses are from ויקרא 14 (39, 44), in the laws of צרעת on houses.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה!
phrases.english: this is returning and this is coming (they are equal)!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 24 that different words cannot be linked.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in Step 24 that פדייה cannot be derived from גאולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דבי רבי ישמעאל linked two different words with the same meaning (שיבה and ביאה), so a difference in wording should not block a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Different words are linked only when no identical word exists
steps.stepSummary: The rule of דבי רבי ישמעאל, that different words can be linked, applies only when no identical word is available. Here מעשר uses the same word as חרמים (גאולה), so we must learn from the identical match.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only where there is nothing that matches it exactly. But where there is something that matches it exactly, we learn from the thing that matches it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 25. Linking two different words, such as שיבה and ביאה, is a fallback that we use only when no identical word exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רבי ישמעאל did link different words. They did so only because no identical word was available. Here חרמים says גאולה and מעשר also says גאולה, so the exact match beats the near match of פדייה by בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only...
Something that matches it exactly
We learn (derive)

phrases.english: This rule applies only
where there is nothing that matches it exactly,
phrases.notes: Then we may link words that are only similar, such as שיבה and ביאה.

phrases.english: but where there is something that matches it exactly,
we learn from the one that matches it.
phrases.notes: So גאולה by חרמים is linked to גאולה by מעשר, not to פדייה by בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25, which was based on the method of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the earlier source: linking non-identical words is only a fallback.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since different words can be linked, פדייה could be linked to גאולה just as well as גאולה to גאולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: An identical word always takes priority, so חרמים is linked to מעשר.

steps.title: Let בכור learn from מעשר through the shared word העברה
steps.stepSummary: בכור and מעשר both use the word העברה. מעשר may not be sold, as it learns from חרמים, so בכור should learn the same ban from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let בכור learn from מעשר through the shared word "passing" (העברה). After all, מעשר itself learns from חרמים through the shared word "redemption" (גאולה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Even if בכור cannot learn directly from חרמים, it could learn indirectly by going through מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By בכור the תורה says "והעברת כל פטר רחם," and by מעשר it says "כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט." Since the two share the word העברה, the selling ban that מעשר received from חרמים should pass on to בכור as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it learn (a challenge: why not derive this?)
Passing: the word used by both בכור and מעשר
It learns (through a גזירה שוה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a chain of two links: חרמים gives to מעשר through גאולה, and then מעשר would give to בכור through העברה. בכור is not being linked directly to חרמים here.

phrases.english: But let the firstborn learn
"passing" / "passing" from the tithe,
phrases.notes: "והעברת" by בכור and "יעבור תחת השבט" by מעשר.

phrases.english: since the tithe also learns
"redemption" / "redemption" from dedications!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that בכור is not linked directly to חרמים, but suggests it can learn indirectly through מעשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the selling ban does not apply to בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second גזירה שוה (העברה) between מעשר and בכור should carry the ban over to בכור.

steps.title: The word הוא by חרמים leaves out בכור
steps.stepSummary: The תורה added the word "הוא" by חרמים to limit the ban to חרמים alone and to leave out בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One limited it by חרמים with the word "it": "it," and not בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of Step 27. A word in the verse about חרמים blocks the ban from spreading to בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse "קדש קדשים הוא לה'" contains the word "הוא," and that word comes to exclude something. The גמרא says it excludes בכור, so any chain that would bring the selling ban to בכור is cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה limited (excluded) something
"It": a limiting word in the verse

phrases.english: The Merciful One limited it regarding dedications,
"it": "it," and not the firstborn.
phrases.notes: From "קדש קדשים הוא לה'" (ויקרא כז:כח).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 by pointing to a limiting word in the verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A מיעוט (exclusion word) in the verse blocks the derivation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בכור would learn the selling ban from מעשר through העברה.

steps.title: Maybe הוא leaves out מעשר instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why "הוא" should exclude בכור. Perhaps it excludes מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: "it," and not מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 28. The word "הוא" does not say which item it excludes, so maybe it excludes מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "הוא" excluded מעשר, then מעשר could be sold. That would undo the whole point that מעשר learns the ban from חרמים.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (proposing the opposite reading)

phrases.english: But say: "it," and not the tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 28's choice of what "הוא" excludes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exclusion word is general, so it could equally exclude מעשר.

steps.title: מעשר shares the word גאולה, so it stays included
steps.stepSummary: מעשר is written with the same word, גאולה, as חרמים, so it is treated like חרמים. That is why "הוא" must exclude בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר is written with "redemption," just like it (חרמים).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 29. Because מעשר uses the same word as חרמים, it counts as "like חרמים," and the exclusion falls on בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as Steps 24 and 26: the closer match wins. מעשר shares גאולה with חרמים, while בכור does not. So the item that is less similar, בכור, is the one that "הוא" excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: Like it, just as it is
Redemption: the word shared by מעשר and חרמים

steps.whatToRemember: The selling ban reaches מעשר, because it shares the word גאולה with חרמים. It does not reach בכור, because "הוא" excludes it and it uses a different word (פדייה).

phrases.english: The tithe has "redemption" written just like it.
phrases.notes: "לא יגאל" appears both by מעשר and by חרמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 29 by showing that מעשר matches חרמים more closely than בכור does.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical preference: the item with the identical word is kept included.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר stays included because of גאולה, and "הוא" excludes בכור.

steps.title: רבא says the words לא יגאל by חרמים are not needed for their plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different approach. The words "לא יגאל" by חרמים are not needed for their plain meaning, so they are free to teach the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: "It shall not be redeemed" by חרמים is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a new approach and states his claim: the words "לא יגאל" by חרמים teach nothing on their own. The next step will show why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה works best when the words used are "free," meaning not needed for their plain meaning. רבא argues that the חרמים side of the link is free, which makes the link with מעשר strong.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall not be redeemed"
Is not needed (so it is free for a derivation)
Items a person devotes to the כהן or to the Temple

phrases.english: Rava said:
"It shall not be redeemed" of dedications is not needed,

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דַּחֲרָמִים לָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to steps 14-20: instead of proving the מעשר side free, רבא shows the חרמים side of the גזירה שוה (step 12) is free, meeting the condition set in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "לא יגאל" by חרמים is not needed for its plain meaning, so it is available for the גזירה שוה with מעשר.

steps.title: Why the words לא יגאל teach nothing about חרמים themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his claim. With the owner, חרמים are already holy (הקדש). With the כהן, they are ordinary (חולין). Either way, a ban on redeeming them adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: For where are they? If they are with the owner, they are holy. If they are with the כהן, they are ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports Step 31. He shows that the words "לא יגאל" have no practical job to do for חרמים themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the item is still with the owner, it already has the status of הקדש, so the owner obviously cannot take it back. Once the item reaches the כהן, it becomes his ordinary property, which he may sell or use freely. Since the words teach nothing in either case, they must be there for something else: the גזירה שוה with מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: In the owner's possession
Holy property
In the כהן's possession
Ordinary, non-holy property

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the words "לא יגאל" by חרמים have no plain job, because before the item reaches the כהן it is הקדש and after it reaches him it is חולין. So the words are free to teach the selling ban for מעשר.

phrases.english: For where are they?
If they are in the owner's possession, they are holy,
phrases.notes: So the owner clearly cannot reclaim or redeem them.

phrases.english: if they are in the priest's possession, they are ordinary.
phrases.notes: So the כהן may do as he wishes with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתַנְהוּ הֵיכָא? אִי בֵּי בְעָלִים — הֶקְדֵּשׁ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבא's claim in Step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That "לא יגאל" by חרמים is not needed for its plain meaning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A two-case argument: with the owner the item is already הקדש, and with the כהן it is חולין, so the ban adds nothing in either case.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the two stages of חרמים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חרמים in the owner's house are like הקדש in every way, and once given to the כהן they are like חולין in every way. Each half is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: חרמים, as long as they are still in the owner's house, are treated like הקדש in every way, because the פסוק says, "Every חרם is most holy to ה׳." Once the owner gives them to the כהן, they are treated like חולין in every way, because the פסוק says, "Every חרם in Israel shall be yours."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as the source for רבא's point from Step 32. The ברייתא shows that חרמים are either fully holy or fully ordinary, depending on who holds them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the owner, the item is already הקדש, so its holiness is already governed by the rules of הקדש. With the כהן, it is plain חולין and his own property, so there is no holiness left for redemption to remove. This sets up רבא's next point: a ban on redeeming חרמים has nothing to add at either stage.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה)
Items a person dedicates with the word חרם; they end up going to the כהנים
The owner's house, meaning the owner still has the item
Property dedicated to the Temple
Ordinary, non-holy property
In every respect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חרמים stop being חרמים when the כהן gets them. The category stays the same. Only the way the law applies changes: the item now acts like ordinary property, because it simply belongs to the כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-stage picture is the base of רבא's whole approach. If neither stage needs a ban on redemption, then the words "לא יגאל" are free to be used for the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Dedications, as long as
they are in the owner's house (possession)
are like consecrated property in all respects,
as it is stated: "Every dedicated item
phrases.notes: ויקרא כז:כח

phrases.english: is most holy to the Lord."
Once he gave them to the priest,
they are like non-sacred property in all respects,
as it is stated: "Every dedicated item in Israel
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:יד

phrases.english: shall be yours."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source for רבא's claim that חרמים are הקדש with the owner and חולין with the כהן.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a ban on redeeming חרמים adds nothing at either stage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא based on ויקרא כז:כח and במדבר יח:יד.

steps.title: רבא begins to apply the ברייתא to the words "לא יגאל"
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts quoting the פסוק "לא ימכר ולא יגאל" so he can show that its words are not needed for their plain meaning. This passage cuts off after the first word.
steps.simpleTranslation: "It may not..."
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא begins quoting the פסוק about חרמים, "לא ימכר ולא יגאל", to apply the ברייתא to it. The full point continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא showed that חרמים are either already הקדש or already חולין, רבא is about to ask what "לא יגאל" could still add. His answer will be that these words are free, so they can be used for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It may not be redeemed (the phrase רבא is about to treat as free for a גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: "It may not...
phrases.notes: Start of the quote "לא ימכר ולא יגאל" (ויקרא כז:כח). It continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא back to the פסוק, so the ברייתא can be used to show that "לא יגאל" is free.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Still in progress: רבא is about to conclude that "לא יגאל" is free to teach the גזירה שוה.
